evidence:
Scope and method: Independently inspected actual frozen WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx using openpyxl, Quality Checks!A28:D28 and Internal Quality Checks!A28:E28. Row 27 says "No criterion enforces something the prompt/professional default never required (no false-fail on correct apps). Reports every instance." The Internal E28 note discusses the house login convention; this task explicitly requests no sign-in and its judges correctly do not require it. Read frozen Harbor SKILL.md, quality-checks.md section 27 (criterion-to-requirement map), staged-task-contract.md, deterministic-checks.md, and current qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md. Policy's "No hidden requirements" says a golden default is not automatically required. All 79 criteria were inspected: 1 Render, 1 Constraints, 64 Functional, 7 Polish, 6 Visual; all five injected prompt templates and app_context.md were read.

One confirmed source-level demand lacks public support: .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task/tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:370 (S16 step 4) says "Reuse S02's already-required four-second successful timer control as the delayed successful comparison" and "The delayed duration should reflect roughly four seconds (a broad 3-8 second range is acceptable)." Its owner is .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:273, cw_console_duration (weight 0.10 of Functional total 32.70). But S02's actual source at prompt.md:148 registers a click handler; the four-second timer is scheduled inside that handler only. The next line, :149, directs a button click after the initial HTML Run completed. Thus the measured four seconds are a later interaction, not the duration of the explicit Run that installed the handler. Public .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task/environment/instructions/behaviour.md:19 asks only "Show how long each run took." Lines 11 and 13 explicitly distinguish a "successfully completed preview" from later interaction and completion of its Run. Neither those notes nor instruction.md, overview.md, ui.md, security.md, policy.md, integration.md or seed_data.json requires replacing a completed Run's duration with the duration of each later preview interaction. A professional playground may preserve its measured per-Run history and display later interaction output without rewriting that history. This is a hidden measurement convention, not a request to waive duration measurement. The fallback at prompt.md:370 runs a real four-second timer only if S02's control cannot complete; it does not accommodate a working control whose completed-Run duration remains short. Nominal above-floor reward exposure is 0.6 * 0.10 / 32.70 = 0.0018348624, hence bounded P2.

Raw evidence was checked rather than adopting a previous review: raw-evidence-index.json binds RESULTS.json SHA256 ec88c00c12336257196e209f427a40690b76b4d3fc7f283656bc67735cf1bc09, independently matched. RESULTS.json's functional/prompt hashes match the frozen task exactly (4b56232c522d4cf1193430fc2200e7d68e53e941e83ee0f13d8e2e56fe66e18c and adc53fbb8d376a7c5396d395ffd72360620b8735231e46dfb87fac8da328aa42). The executed drivers/current_flow.cjs:19 calls d.run(code,'css-timer.html') first, starts timerStart afterward, then clicks Queue timer and records success-delayed. drivers/repair_flow.cjs:3-9 compares that interval against the displayed duration and requires 3000-8000 ms. Driver hashes independently match RESULTS.json: current_flow.cjs 01993eccc46444674d0dc281deff72ed1d73e74b7a053b76c2eb0bc71e39d613; repair_flow.cjs 99d799b14ff5a3d9f2c206a388aff35458799b3e2cc1f85e090fa13f8f6bce1f. The raw S16.console_duration evidence reports 5.8 ms for a short Run and 4001.3 ms for the delayed interaction against observed 4085.120337 ms. That establishes the golden's particular convention, not a public requirement.

Read-only witness execution: invoked the unmodified repair_flow.cjs exports with Node on synthetic observation traces, making no task edits or browser/provider calls. A measured short Run of 6.1 ms (90 ms browser observation), followed by a correctly retained completed HTML-Run duration of 5.8 ms while its later interaction takes 4085 ms, yields S16.console_duration=false. Replacing only the delayed label with 4001.3 ms yields true. These are predicate-level counterexamples, not claimed end-to-end app or configured-judge runs. The golden observation is real; whether an actual configured judge would wrongly reject the conforming alternate app remains unmeasured.

Reverse map for the remaining demands: Render's authored DOM/log Run maps to instruction.md:1,7 and overview.md:3; Constraints' successful health and fresh-context server write/read maps to integration.md:5 and overview.md:7, with identity/exact fields from behaviour.md:25. S01 maps to overview.md:3,9; S02 maps to overview.md:5 and behaviour.md:5; S03/S04 map to behaviour.md:7,11,13; S05 to security.md:3; S07 to security.md:9 and policy.md:5; S08 to security.md:7; S09/S36 to behaviour.md:9 and security.md:5; S10-S13 error messages/one-based source positions map to behaviour.md:15, rollback to :13, ordinary recovery to instruction.md:3 and policy.md:5. S14-S16 console levels/inspection/history/clear and genuine per-Run duration map to behaviour.md:19. S17 maps to behaviour.md:21, S19 to ui.md:5. S21/S22 map to behaviour.md:25, security.md:11 and integration.md:7. S23 maps directly to behaviour.md:29; S24 to :27; S34 to ui.md:9, with draft/output preservation an ordinary non-destructive theme-switch expectation. Polish controls/navigation/narrow-screen usability map to ui.md:3,7,9 and instruction.md:7. Visual's readable, coherent layout/theme treatment is covered by ui.md:9 and ordinary professional presentation; anchors expressly accept native components/simple styles. No extra identity surface, import/export feature, exact API schema, fixed palette, preferred editor package, required indentation width, exact control label, specific initial theme or documented editor-escape shortcut was demanded. Positive controls are genuine controls for their named negative outcomes, not an added technology mandate. Only the timing convention above was established as an unrequired demand; no task source was changed.
counterexample: False-fail witness: An otherwise conforming playground measures and keeps each explicit Run's own elapsed duration, including timers scheduled by that Run. S02's HTML Run installs its button and finishes in 5.8 ms. A later click runs the allowed four-second timer correctly, records both expected markers, updates the successful preview, and remains cancellable; the UI retains "Run completed in 5.8 ms" rather than relabeling that completed Run as four seconds. Nothing public requires interaction-duration display, yet S16:370 and its reproduced scripted predicate reject it. False-pass witness for the same probe: an app measures successful explicit Runs incorrectly when they schedule pending timers, freezing the displayed duration at their initial synchronous work, but separately overwrites duration after post-completion button interactions. The selected short-Run/interaction pair (6.1 ms and 4001.3 ms) passes the inspected S16 predicate without exercising a successful explicit Run that itself schedules the delay. Both are concrete implementation alternatives evaluated as synthetic traces; neither is claimed to have been installed or graded end to end.
suggested_fix: In S16 use a genuine successful delayed Run whose top-level source schedules the four-second timer, and compare that Run's duration with the short Run; do not require a completed Run's duration to be replaced by later interaction timing. Update the focused golden driver accordingly and verify the conforming stable-per-Run-duration alternative. Keep the existing public contract, weights and shared harness unchanged.
